Step 1 · Fig 1 · Supplementary Fig 1

Genome-scale identification of chemoresistance genes

Fig 1 title, as published. Thirty genome-scale screens in six cell lines: how many genes pass the chemoresistance threshold in each, how the screens correlate, and the IC50 of every drug in every line.

Step 2 · Fig 2 · Supplementary Fig 3

A systematic view on chemoresistance genes

Fig 2 title, as published. Enriched terms per drug, the enrichment ratios of Fig 2d and the chemosensitizer genes. The TCGA panels (Fig 2e, f) are not part of this page.

Step 3 · Fig 3 · Supplementary Figs 4g, 5

Rapid derivation of chemoresistant cells

Fig 3 title, as published. IC50 of each knockout-derived and drug-selected resistant line, the cell numbers of Fig 3f and h, and nine ΔTP53 clones followed for nine days.

Step 4 · Fig 4 · Supplementary Figs 6, 7

Cellular and molecular features of oxaliplatin-resistant cells

Fig 4 title, as published. Growth, cell cycle and apoptosis of the oxaliplatin-resistant HCT116 lines and the irinotecan-resistant DLD1 lines, and the overlap of their differentially expressed genes.

Step 5 · Fig 5 · Supplementary Figs 10, 13

Interrogation of druggable targets against oxaliplatin resistance by second-round CRISPR screens

Fig 5 title, as published. The druggable-gene hits in six resistant lines, PLK4 knockout and rescue, and the PLK4 inhibitor CFI-400945 across seven HCT116-based and three further resistant lines.

Step 6 · Fig 6 · Supplementary Fig 14

Selective dependency on PLK4 for oxaliplatin-resistant cells

Fig 6 title, as published. Cell cycle, spindle collapse, centrosome number, polyploidy and apoptosis after PLK4 knockout or CFI-400945.

Step 7 · Fig 7a–c · Supplementary Fig 16

Validation of efficacy of the PLK4 inhibitor CFI-400945 against oxaliplatin resistance in mice and at clinical levels

Fig 7 title, as published. This page covers the xenografts in mice (Fig 7a–c, Supplementary Fig 16). The patient tissue and organoid panels (Fig 7d–g) are not included.
